profile: Classic Bedrock 26.60 component profiles, fixed GUI scale 2; game routing, player data and actual 3D skin rendering supplied by host
scope: Four reusable controls. Original PNG identity and explicit JSON declarations are verified separately from responsive screen layout, native renderer output and Web input behavior.

web.disabledBannerContentSize: 92% x 90% of outer surface, source offset (14px,0), vertically centered
web.buttonCaptionShadow: none, as declared by common_buttons.new_ui_binding_button_label; actual caption overrides inherited shared Button Web profile.
web.disabledVisibleAlignment: Visible avatar/name are vertically centered in an exact 36 CSS px inner line, mathematically equivalent to centered source content while avoiding intermediate 90%-height DOM quantization.

PlayerList.behavior: Native buttons in a vertically labeled toolbar, roving ArrowUp/Down/Home/End skips disabled rows. Enter/Space and pointer selection report player ID. Controlled selectedId keeps ownership with host. Invite callback is optional; absent callback omits invite button.
limits: The native action opens a player profile card; persistent selectedId is an application state extension and does not invent a persistent selected skin. aria-current identifies host selection.

Online/offline status text is an explicit host extension. The Classic pause player row contains a gamertag and platform/local icon, not this second status line. Supplying no online property preserves the one-line source profile.
Avatar PNG/React slot and platform icon are caller supplied. No portrait, skin, gamertag or network presence is fabricated.

Permission button, friends drawer, engine-specific gamerpic visibility and disabled-banner bindings are not implemented as multiplayer transport. Disabled Web rows use the source banner skin and native disabled semantics.

Flattening includes both common.new_ui_button_panel content inset (3 game px) and pause.player_button_content inset/offset, not just the leaf controls. Disabled banner uses its independent 92%/90% layout; avatar and name remain aligned.

The reusable list omits social controls, disconnected/IP labels and their surrounding trailing spacers; bottom padding is explicitly zero. Disabled MainBannersHover paints its full outer rectangle without the active button border.

source: Original 22x22 action PNGs and pressed variants
Installed Classic HUD/touch texture inventory; no public native layout/input algorithm was found in hud_screen.json

nativeAssets.sourceAlpha: Original PNG alpha is unchanged. Sprint includes a real disabled PNG.

web.movement: Unit-circle normalized x right-positive / y forward-negative; diagonal keyboard vectors normalize to length 1.

TouchControls.behavior: Every pointer ID owns a held-action source. Two pointers holding the same action emit one down and one final up. Pointer up/cancel/lost capture, disabling, removing an action and unmount release held state. Joystick captures its first pointer, clamps its vector, and returns to zero on release/cancel/lost capture/unmount. Native buttons also support held Space/Enter and joystick Arrow keys; blur releases keyboard holds. Assistive click produces a down/up pulse. No global OS key injection or network action is performed.
limits: No invented D-pad glyphs or Java atlas UV are used. Only the original standalone joystick/action PNGs are painted. A D-pad variant is deferred until its Bedrock resource/UV behavior can be established.

Bitmap dimensions do not prove native control positions, GUI scale, joystick travel/deadzone, finger sliding policy, alpha settings or engine gesture arbitration. All current slot spacing and input policy are explicitly Web reconstruction.
Opacity defaults to preserving original asset alpha, not an asserted native touch-opacity setting. No synthetic disabled artwork is drawn.
The CSS grid may wrap as a group but the 128/64/44px source-profile regions never shrink to fit; no animation or hidden timer is added.

web.footerGlyphFit: contain centered inside the declared source image box, preserving actual PNG aspect
web.buttonCaptionShadow: none, as declared by common_buttons.new_ui_binding_button_label; actual caption overrides inherited shared Button Web profile.

PauseMenu.behavior: All menu actions are typed callbacks. Main actions support ArrowUp/Down/Home/End focus and native button activation. Escape invokes resume only while focus is in the component and resume is enabled. autoFocus is opt-in for embedded galleries. Disabled actions and full disabled mode block routes; full disabled also disables supplied player rows and invite.

nativeObservation.observed: Four primary buttons, three footer icons and a paper-doll/dressing-room area are visible. The native current singleplayer branch has a top-right social drawer, no inline legacy player sidebar. No unmasked native-to-browser frame equality is claimed.

limits: The 960x540 canvas is a Web default, not a native fixed screen dimension. Callers can set finite width/height; percent layout is an explicit source-layout reconstruction pending native viewport/anchor calibration.

The optional players prop composes the legacy 150-game-pixel info panel. It is not asserted to be the active 26.60 singleplayer social-drawer layout. Native friends drawer, announcements, trial/editor branches and controller helpers are deferred.
The optional logo is host art. The demo uses the actual original title.png, kept outside library textures; no Minecraft logo is required or bundled by the library component itself.

skinRenderer is a host React slot. There is no CSS/sprite imitation of the native 3D paper doll. Empty slots remain empty; optional playerName is an explicitly labeled host-text reconstruction of a native custom name tag.
When a legacy sidebar is explicitly composed, the host skin area is shifted left by its 300px width to avoid overlap; this extra composition rule is not a source-native screen certification.
Shared Button skins implement Web states. The source footer pressed_alpha=.65 is recorded, but its native shader/content/border propagation is not certified by these component states.

The footer JSON declares image boxes, not source pixel aspect ratios: achievements PNG is 32x32 and camera PNG14x11. Native lossless capture shows preserved shape. The browser profile uses centered contain; an explicit keep_ratio default is not proven solely by these JSON declarations.

web.gradient: Vertical CSS interpolation of the two declared source endpoints; data-fidelity=renderer-reconstruction
web.buttonCaptionShadow: none, as declared by common_buttons.new_ui_binding_button_label; actual caption overrides inherited shared Button Web profile.

DeathScreen.behavior: ready/loading is controlled by the host. Respawn/quit visibility and enabled state are independent props and use native buttons with typed callbacks. loading omits title/action controls and exposes a status label. No automatic respawn, timers, game save, command engine or routing is performed.
limits: Classic death_screen.json has no score label. The optional score/scoreLabel region is explicitly data-source=host-extension and absent unless supplied.

The source custom gradient gives endpoint RGBA but no exposed interpolation direction, color-space policy or premultiplied quantization. CSS vertical interpolation is a declared renderer reconstruction, not an original PNG or native-frame proof.
DeathScreen is a reusable canvas/region, not a modal focus trap; the host owns scene placement, page/game input ownership and screen route state.
The final 20-game-pixel labels spacer is a stack child, not container padding. This preserves title/reason percentages against the full H/2 labels panel.

variant=classic selects the older JSON profile. Default native uses independently identified installed HTML UI geometry, palette and typography. Browser/native text, radial gradient and underlying world/HUD rasterization remains outside complete frame equivalence.

nativeRuntimeObservation.result: Active installed gameplay.html loads the HTML UI gameplay bundle. Its death component, typography, palette and rem scaling explain the captured runtime. Native is now the default; variant=classic retains the old resource JSON profile.

nativeProfile.entry: gameplay.html -> gameplay bundle -> HN death view; BN CSS mapping; gc guiScale; IP vanilla palette; cm/hm/ym buttons; tu Typography

guiScale.remCss: 5 * guiScale; local CSS custom property only
guiScale.source: gc sets documentElement fontSize to 5*guiScale; this component scopes the unit to itself.

typography.fallback: Open library font through --mc-font. Supply separately licensed original families for native text metrics.

nativeProfile.scope: Controlled ready/loading content, native HTML button behavior and host callbacks. No engine retry/timing/routing/world renderer. Score is an absent-by-default host extension. Original fonts are optional caller/local-preview inputs. Whole native-frame equality is not claimed.

loadingIndicator.publication: Private installed GIF is not redistributed. Optional loadingIndicator caller slot; no fabricated replacement. Default exposes the source body status without a spinner.

behavior.escape: Native ready routes component-scoped Escape to onQuit only when quit is visible/enabled; host onKeyDown can preventDefault. Loading does not route Escape. No document/global keyboard listener.
behavior.quitLabel: Game menu for native; Main menu for classic; explicit quitLabel overrides either.
behavior.loadingIndicator: Optional host slot for the licensed original GIF; animation belongs to supplied content. The component owns no animation timers or engine retries.

boundaries: All PNGs preserve original Mojang ownership and bytes, including intrinsic alpha. New controls do not relicense assets as MIT artwork.

Normal/large font sizes inherit existing Text CSS variables. The optional Mojangles profile is 20/40/60px; base library variables are 18/36/54px. Source font enums and shadow flags do not alone prove numeric browser font metrics.
Only explicit geometry and decoded original resources can be source-certified here. Web input handling, host extensions and reconstructed native custom-renderer output are labeled separately.
Callbacks never inject global operating-system keyboard input or perform multiplayer/server operations. DOM reads occur only after mount or inside input events.
